open_points.text: one elapsed reading per viewer-entry request
open_points.question: Which incoming requests count as viewer-entry requests for CLK-002: every request targeting the entry route, including one rejected by an earlier transport check, or only requests that reach the entry rate limiter after those checks?
options: Read the elapsed clock once for every request targeting the viewer-entry route, even if trusted-host, method, body-size, or decoding checks reject it first.
Read the elapsed clock once only when a request reaches the viewer-entry rate-limit check; earlier transport refusals read it zero times.
open_points.default_guess: Count only requests that reach the viewer-entry rate limiter, because the elapsed reading exists solely to measure that limiter's window.

witness.initial: The viewer-entry limiter is below its limit, and the clock source records every monotonic read.
events: A client sends a request targeting viewer entry with an untrusted Host value.
The transport guard rejects the request under the trusted-host policy.
outcomes: An implementation treating the route target as sufficient reads the monotonic clock once before returning the rejection.
An implementation treating only rate-limiter invocations as viewer-entry requests returns the same rejection without reading the monotonic clock.
witness.observer: The CLK-002 transport-guard verification sees a monotonic-read count of one or zero.
